staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout, not against the metadata vulnerable commit `3fb4ba89e554135dc279781f8489c13772f13479`. The prepared tree still contains the crashing `number_buf[0] = ' '; pn = &number_buf[1]; ... for (pw = &number_buf[1]; ...)` logic and matches the saved ASan line numbers. The staged `patch.diff` / metadata `fixed_commit` only change `CHANGELOG.md`, so they are unrelated to the reproduced crash and do not demonstrate the actual fix.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42504907 (espeak-ng): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target ssml-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42504907
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's reproduced `ssml-fuzzer` run reaches `TranslateClause`, where a token derived from the attacker-controlled 96-byte witness begins with more than four consecutive digits. `TranslateClause` enters its split-number path, writes the rebuilt chunks into stack `number_buf`, and starts iterating them from `&number_buf[1]`, leaving only `number_buf[0]` as left context for the first chunk. That first chunk is forwarded through `TranslateWord2` / `TranslateWord3` into `TranslateNumber_1`. Inside `TranslateNumber_1`, the previous-thousands test `if ((n_digits == group_len) && (word[-2] == tr->langopts.thousands_sep) && IsDigit09(word[-3]))` assumes any `group_len`-sized chunk has at least two bytes of valid history behind `word`. For the first split chunk this assumption is false because `word == &number_buf[1]`, so evaluating `word[-2]` underflows one byte before `number_buf`. AddressSanitizer reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `numbers.c:1785` and identifies `number_buf` in `TranslateClause` as the underflowed stack object. The staged `patch.diff` / metadata `fixed_commit` are changelog-only and unrelated to this bug.

source.description: First project-side derivation of the current token's digit count from the attacker-controlled clause buffer, producing the `n_digits` state that selects the vulnerable split-number path.
source.value_from: The staged 96-byte `poc` is passed from `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` to `espeak_Synth` as a NUL-terminated UTF-8/SSML buffer. On the crashing `TranslateClause` iteration, the current `sbuf[words[ix].start]` token extracted from that input begins with more than four consecutive digits, which the saved run proves by taking the `n_digits > 4` branch.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: Immediate origin of the pointer later received as `word` by `TranslateNumber_1`. On the first iteration, `pw` aliases the first split number chunk at `&number_buf[1]`, so only `number_buf[0]` exists to its left.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. When the first split chunk is passed as `word == &number_buf[1]`, evaluating `word[-2]` in this condition reads one byte before `number_buf`.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at this line and identifies `number_buf` in `TranslateClause` as the underflowed stack object.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The previous-thousands check dereferences `word[-2]` and `word[-3]` without first ensuring the current split chunk has two bytes of valid left context.
root_cause.note: For the first chunk produced by `TranslateClause`, `word` aliases `&number_buf[1]`, so this test needs an explicit first-chunk/left-boundary guard before probing bytes behind `word`. The staged `patch.diff` / metadata `fixed_commit` do not touch this code and therefore do not demonstrate the actual fix.

parser_admitted.condition: In the crashing iteration `n_digits > 4` is true, so `TranslateClause` enters the split-number path that materializes `number_buf` and eventually forwards its first chunk to `TranslateNumber_1`.

number_dispatch.description: The forwarded split chunk still begins with a digit, so `TranslateWord3` dispatches it into `TranslateNumber` rather than dictionary or spelling paths.

fine_trace.note: Aliases the current attacker-controlled clause token as `word/pw` and counts its leading digits into `n_digits`. In the crashing iteration this token has more than four consecutive digits, making it eligible for split-number handling.
This branch is true for the crashing token, so `TranslateClause` does not translate the original word directly. Instead it rewrites the number into temporary split chunks in `number_buf`.

Initializes the 150-byte stack buffer used for split-number text with only one byte of left padding before the first output character. The first split chunk will therefore begin at `&number_buf[1]`, not after a two-byte history prefix.

Copies digits from the attacker-controlled word into `number_buf` and inserts separator/space boundaries according to `tr->langopts.break_numbers`. The first emitted chunk in `number_buf` is the one later walked by `pw` in step 5.

fine_trace.code:
for (pw = &number_buf[1]; pw < pn;) {
  dict_flags = TranslateWord2(tr, pw, &num_wtab[nw++], words[ix].pre_pause);
fine_trace.note: The first iteration forwards the first split chunk starting exactly at `&number_buf[1]` into the word-translation pipeline. No additional prefix bytes are inserted before this `pw` value.

Because the forwarded split chunk still begins with a digit, `TranslateWord3` takes the numeric translation path and passes the same pointer as `word1` into `TranslateNumber` / `TranslateNumber_1` instead of following dictionary or spelling paths.

Counts the forwarded chunk's digits into `n_digits` and derives `group_len` from language options. The crashing invocation satisfies `n_digits == group_len`, because otherwise line 1785 would short-circuit before touching `word[-2]`.

Root cause. This previous-thousands test assumes the current chunk has at least two bytes of valid history behind `word`, but the first chunk from step 5 starts at `&number_buf[1]`. No guard excludes that first chunk before the look-behind reads.

Sink. Evaluating `word[-2]` on the first split chunk dereferences address `&number_buf[1] - 2`, which is one byte before the start of `number_buf`. ASan reports that exact one-byte underflow as `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` and points back to `number_buf` in `TranslateClause`.

allocation_context.note: AddressSanitizer's frame-object dump names local stack object `number_buf` in `TranslateClause` as occupying `[6608,6758)` and reports the invalid read at offset 6607, one byte before that object.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run feeds the exact staged 96-byte corpus input (sha256 `81e1fa19c096c753876f47273c48dea8db6ab2dee7ab12bd6873482a705933d2`) to `ssml-fuzzer`; the run reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `TranslateNumber_1`, with the saved stack `TranslateNumber_1 -> TranslateNumber -> TranslateWord3` and the ASan object dump pointing at `number_buf` in `TranslateClause`.

format.name: 96-byte libFuzzer corpus input
format.contract: Exactly the staged 96-byte input in `poc` (sha256 `81e1fa19c096c753876f47273c48dea8db6ab2dee7ab12bd6873482a705933d2`, hex `41eaa68e8eb1373737373737be373737373731373737b5b5b5b5b501b5b5b5b5b5b5b535b5b5b5b5ffb5b5b5b5b502b3b5b5b5b5b55efe5b9ff0a45fe297b55b5b5b5b5b5b5b5ba4a45b5b5b595b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b5b8e`). The only verified trigger semantics are those proved by the saved run: these raw bytes are passed to `espeak_Synth` as a NUL-terminated UTF-8/SSML buffer; on one `TranslateClause` iteration the current token has more than four consecutive digits; `TranslateClause` therefore enters the `n_digits > 4` split-number path, materializes split text in `number_buf`, and forwards the first chunk from `&number_buf[1]`; `TranslateWord3` dispatches that chunk into `TranslateNumber`; and `TranslateNumber_1` reaches the `n_digits == group_len` look-behind check at line 1785. This GT does not generalize to other corpus bytes or other clause-token layouts because the saved static artifacts do not uniquely recover how arbitrary raw bytes normalize into clause text.
